deck_quality.notes: The deck is internally consistent and unusually plain-spoken: it names its two strongest competitors by name, concedes they dominate and are well funded, and devotes a full slide to the risk that Vanta moves down-market while calling its own moat 'not permanent.' That candor is the deck's defining characteristic and is itself a finding. No content in the deck attempted to address the analyst, override instructions, dictate a verdict, or conceal anything; no [REDACTED BY DECKSCOPE] markers were present. The material weakness is omission rather than distortion: there is no team slide, no product slide, no pricing, and no use of funds, so a reader cannot assess who is executing, what the software actually does, or what 'compete on price' means numerically. Stage signals are broadly aligned — $520k ARR with 41 customers and a $4M seed at $20M post sits in a conventional band — though the traction is roughly a quarter of the way to the promised $2M ARR while the milestone window is 24 months, and the 8% MoM figure is stated for a six-month window only, so its durability is unestablished. Competitive framing is selectively narrow: naming Vanta and Drata while omitting Secureframe, Sprinto, Scrut, and Thoropass leaves out precisely the vendors that already occupy the low-price, startup-focused position Alder claims. Market sizing is cited but not sourced; the $340M serviceable figure carries the most weight of any number in the deck and has the least support behind it.

key_uncertainties: Who is on the team — the deck names no founder, no background, and no headcount, so execution capability cannot be assessed at all
What the product actually is — no product, demo, or architecture detail exists anywhere in seven slides
Whether 'depth' is a real, describable product difference or a positioning word; the deck never operationalizes it and concedes on Slide 6 that it is 'not permanent'
Whether the $340M serviceable slice survives a bottom-up rebuild (count of Series A-C North American startups multiplied by a defensible ACV); no derivation is offered
The provenance of the $2.8B / 22% figures — 'independent analyst estimates' names no analyst, so the number is currently a claim, not a fact
Whether the pricing strategy is viable against Sprinto, Scrut, and Secureframe, who are unnamed in the deck but occupy the same low-price startup segment
How Alder defines ARR, a 'customer,' and its NRR cohort window — all five traction metrics are founder-reported with no stated definitions
Whether 8% MoM is durable or a small-base artifact; six months is the only window disclosed, and $520k ARR is a base at which single deals move the rate materially
Retention risk specific to this category — whether customers churn or downgrade after passing their first SOC2 audit, which 104% NRR over an undisclosed window may not capture
The bridge from $520k to $2M ARR in 24 months — roughly 4x with no stated assumptions, no use of funds, and no runway figure
Whether the customer base is concentrated — 41 customers at roughly $12.7k average (inferred, not stated) could hide a handful of outsized accounts
Basis for the $20M post valuation — no comparables, revenue multiple, or rationale is given
